headline: Approved pay rate ordinances for Teamsters Local 251 and Local 3960; denied several damage claims and referred them to outside parties.
summary: The council approved the second reading of a pay rate ordinance for Local 251 and passed the first reading of a pay rate ordinance for Local 3960, which adds a Parking Enforcement Officer. It denied several damage claims and sent requests to RI Energy, the RI Department of Transportation, and city departments about Smithfield Avenue and Moshassuck Industrial Highway.
decisions: Approved the records of the September 23, 2026 Finance Committee and City Council meetings as prepared by the Clerk.
Approved the consent agenda by unanimous voice vote, filing communications and referring several items.
Referred a request for an easement for Rhode Island Energy to install an electric utility pole at 100 Freight Street to the City Property Committee.
Referred the Pericles Vieira damage claim of $1,349.08 to the Committee on Claims and Pending Suits.
Referred three damage claims, including $2,347,000.00+ from Lynn Farinelli, to the Law Department and RI Interlocal Trust.
Approved a request to RI Energy and the RI Department of Transportation to investigate vibrations on Smithfield Avenue, passed on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved a request to the police, Public Works, and Zoning about illegal parking, speeding, and dumping on Moshassuck Industrial Highway, passed on a unanimous voice vote.
Approved RI Energy petition for installation at Freight Street, pending approval from the Director of Public Works.
Confirmed Patricia Martinez to the Personnel Board, 6-1.
Confirmed Jane Larson to the Advisory Commission on Arts and Culture, 7-0.
Confirmed Elizabeth Crowley to the Planning Commission, 6-1.
Confirmed Nancy T. Pelletier to the Purchasing Board, 6-1.
Confirmed James Bradford to the Water Supply Board, 6-1.
Confirmed Paula A. McAloon to the Zoning Board of Appeals, 6-1.
Confirmed Maribel Echeverry McLaughlin to the Juvenile Hearing Board, 7-0.
Confirmed Marilee E. Arsenault to the Board of Canvassers as an alternate Democratic member, 6-1.
Approved second reading of ordinance setting Local 251 (Teamsters 2026-2029) pay rates, 7-0.
Passed first reading of ordinance setting Local 3960 pay rates to add Parking Enforcement Officer, 7-0.
Approved two damage claims: Cody Tavares by Progressive Subrogation for $1,301.83 and Antonia Ramos & Gerson Dos Santos for $2,100.00, 7-0.
Denied five damage claims and referred them to JR Vinagro Construction Corporation, 7-0.
Denied the $266.19 tire damage claim by Sherry Marshall and referred it to the Providence & Worcester Railroad Company, 7-0.

City Council, October 7, 2026 
 
 D. Communication from the Honorable Marlena Martins Stachowiak, 6 th District 
Councilor, to the Honorable Terrence E. Mercer, City Coun cil President 
(Smithfield Avenue Roadwork) was READ AND ORDERED FILED. 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR STACHOWIAK 
 
With majority consent of the Council, the following motion made by Councilor Stachowiak, 
seconded by Councilor Araujo, was PASSED on a unanimous voice vote: 
  
The Clerk was instructed to send a communication to RI Energy and the RI Department of 
Transportation, requesting that they look into the concerns of the residents and businesses on 
that portion of Smithfield Avenue from about 160 Smithf ield Avenue down close to the 
Providence line, which had utility work done on it by RI Energy.  The concerns stem from 
significant vibrations felt by residents in their homes when trucks drive over that  portion of 
the road.  This has been an ongoing problem  for several months  since the road work was 
done.  Even after re -patching, the problems persist.  The shaking has disturbed some 
resident’s ability to get a good night’s sleep.    Some residents have detected damage to their 
homes, which they fear may be caused by the vibrations.  
 
The council request ed that a comprehensive investigation be done of the affected section of 
Smithfield Avenue and a plan to correct the problems be found.  The hope is that these issues 
will be corrected before the weather turns too cold to make any necessary repairs. 
  
 
 E. Communication from the Honorable Marlena Martins Stachowiak, 6 th District 
Councilor, to the Honorable Terrence E. Mercer, City Council President 
(Moshassuck Industrial Highway) was READ AND ORDERED FILED. 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR STACHOWIAK 
 
With majority consent of the Council, the following motion made by Councilor Stachowiak, 
seconded by Councilor Gregor, was PASSED on a unanimous voice vote: 
  
The Clerk was instructed to send a communication to Chief Ti na Goncalves, Pawtucket 
Police Department ; Chris Crawley, Acting Director of Public Works ; and Carl Johnson, 
Zoning Director ; addressing concerns regarding the illegal parking of large trucks and 
trailers, unattended trailers being left along the roadway, people working on their vehicles 
and leaving puddles of fluids on the street, speeding, illegal dumping and littering on and 
around the Moshassuck Industrial Highway near Galego Park and NETTTS . The Council 
requested that the police strictly enforce the parking ordinances, including, but not limited to 
the overnight parking ordinance for large trucks ; as well as the speeding and dumping laws  
and provide an enhanced police presence to eliminate these issues .  They also requested that   
the Zoning Department c ite violators for illegal dumping in the area, and DPW make sure 
there is proper signage on the highway, and clean the area.
